artifacts.summary: Confirms both systemd units already verify clean and check-extension-docs.sh's core row already passes; verifies at the code level that all four claude-refresh.sh passes run unconditionally through the timer's single --dry-run ExecStart; recommends adding ConditionPathExists to the service unit for the deploy-path gap; and recommends a single small pass-inventory table (name/gate/destructive) added to SKILL.md and refresh.md rather than a rewrite of the existing step-by-step content.

memory_candidates.content: systemd Condition*= directives (e.g. ConditionPathExists) cause a unit to be skipped (informational log, not counted as a failure in systemctl --failed) rather than fail, when the condition evaluates false. For an unattended/no-confirmation timer-triggered oneshot service whose ExecStart target may not exist on every machine (e.g. a gitignored, regenerated deploy tree), adding a matching ConditionPathExists is a low-cost way to convert a silent/failed-unit outcome into a clean skip.

check-extension-docs.sh refuses to run from the agent-system/extensions/ source-store tree itself (its relative path math assumes a deployed .claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ location); it must be invoked against the deployed tree (bash .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh) to get a real PASS/FAIL result. Its overall exit code reflects ALL extensions' status, so a single unrelated extension's FAIL does not mean the extension you actually edited regressed -- check that extension's own PASS/FAIL row in the per-extension summary table, not just the final exit code.
